citeinfo.othercit: Suggested Citation: Authors: Alaska Wildland Fire Coordinating Group, State of Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Forestry and Fire Protection, US Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management, Alaska Fire Service. Title: Alaska Statewide Fire History Location Points. Year : 2024. Publisher: Bureau of Land Management. Access Information: https://fire.ak.blm.gov/predsvcs/maps.php

descript.abstract: Wildland fire history data is made up of wildland fire locations (fire occurrence points) and wildland fire perimeter polygons. Alaska Fire History Points is a time series of reported wildland fires in each calendar year across Alaska. This dataset represents location points of wildfires that are ignited naturally (e.g., lightning) or by humans (including prescribed fires). The dataset includes some, but not all, historical (fires declared ‘out’ in calendar years prior to the current year) wildland fires and is subject to revision. There is no lower size limit for fires to be included and as such, reported 'false alarms' are included. The accuracy of the point locations range in quality because of inconsistencies in the number of significant digits recorded for both latitude and longitude coordinates. Users should be aware that there are many of the fires between 1961 and 1968 are missing fire reports. Data are available as ArcGIS Server Map and Feature Services https://fire.ak.blm.gov/arcgis/rest/services/MapAndFeatureServices and for download from https://fire.ak.blm.gov/predsvcs/maps.php
descript.purpose: This dataset is used to display the fire occurrence points of historical wildland fires within Alaska on maps. These data are subject to revision.
descript.supplinf: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Alaska Fire Service manages a comprehensive Fire History (points and polygons) dataset for Alaska.
